A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same AllPath research. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text and appendices; differences are confined to the arXiv stamp and the response displayed in Figure 11.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on POPE, MCQ-POPE, CHAIR, and MME, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, attention-path analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments and appendix analyses, including results for LLaVA and Qwen models, and revises one qualitative output.

M1.justification: The T2T/I2T scoring, head selection, and intervention procedures in Sections 2–4, including the Qwen adaptation in Appendix C.1, are unchanged.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is identical across the main text and appendices. Figure 11 retains the same image and captioning prompt; replacing its response introduces no new test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline membership, including vanilla, VCD, ICD, PAI, and AD-HH where originally evaluated. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, model configurations, head-identification samples, and decoding settings are unchanged. No revised experimental procedure is reported for the replaced Figure 11 response.

E4.justification: The CHAIR success case in Figure 11 is revised by replacing the displayed AllPath response, changing its qualitative evidence of hallucination mitigation. Ablations, pathway analyses, other examples, and the failure case remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Table 2's averages over three test runs and sample standard deviations. No run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation information is added.

E6.justification: In v1, Figure 11's AllPath output repeats the baseline description, including 'potted plants' and two additional dogs. In v2, it describes the dog, bench, and flower garden without those assertions. All numerical results and other reported outputs are unchanged.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions and equations for attention, LPI, T2T/I2T scores, and intervention scaling are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about multiple causal pathways, format-dependent head behavior, and hallucination mitigation.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 already describes Figure 11 as successfully avoiding hallucination in v1; that interpretation is unchanged in v2. Mechanism explanations, the failure-case discussion, and Appendix E's limitations are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, sampling and decoding instructions, model-specific adaptations, and project access information are identical.

R1.justification: The references, related-work discussion, and positioning against previous intervention and contrastive-decoding approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 21 November 2025 to v2 dated 6 January 2026. Expository prose and section organization are unchanged; the replacement in Figure 11 is reported model output.

P2.justification: Figure 11 retains its image, attention maps, labels, caption, highlighting scheme, and panel arrangement; only the reported response text changes. Other figures, tables, and page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 labels Figure 11 a success while displaying the same hallucinated response for the baseline and AllPath, contradicting Appendix D.2. The replacement response in v2 resolves this local inconsistency and makes the qualitative illustration support its discussion. The benefit is limited because the methods, quantitative evidence, and remaining analyses are unchanged.
